task:
Table of contents ids behave differently between the toc directive and add_toc_hook, and both can overwrite ids. Fix all of these. In the examples below, md = create_markdown(escape=False, plugins=[FencedDirective([TableOfContents()])]), with FencedDirective and TableOfContents from mistune.directives. The sequences stand for line breaks. The toc directive ignores ids already present in raw HTML. Rendering '
```{toc} ``` # title ' must give

title

and href="#toc_1_2". The id must skip every taken value in sequence, the way add_toc_hook's automatic ids already do. The toc directive overwrites an id that a heading already has. Suppose an earlier hook, added with md.before_render_hooks.insert(0, hook), sets token['attrs']['id'] = 'existing' on each heading token. Rendering '```{toc} ``` # title ' must give

title

and href="#existing", and the text id="toc_1" must not appear. add_toc_hook overwrites an existing id too. With md = create_markdown(escape=False), append the same id-setting hook to md.before_render_hooks, then call add_toc_hook(md). After html, state = md.parse('# title '), html must contain

title

, and render_toc_ul(state.env['toc_items']) must contain href="#existing". Two toc sections in one document must share the ids. Rendering '```{toc} ``` ```{toc} ``` # title ' must contain

title

exactly once and href="#toc_1" exactly twice. A custom heading_id function passed to add_toc_hook still produces exactly the ids it returns, with no uniqueness suffix. Everything else must keep working.
